source: Shem Tov Hebrew Matthew (Even Bochan, Ibn Shaprut c. 1385; critical text ed. G. Howard, base ms British Library Add. 26964)

verses.translation: At that{H1931} time{H6256} Herodos the tetrarka heard{H8085} reports{H8052} of Yeshua{H3442}.

translation_notes: טיטרא״קה — the Greek title τετράρχης ('tetrarch') transliterated and flagged as foreign with scribal gershayim, exactly as the text marks its other loanwords (evangeli, Antichristos): in this text Greek officialdom is the visitor, Hebrew the host.
textual_notes: Shem Tov's own section heading פרק ס״ה (Perek 65) begins here.
Howard's apparatus (14:1): טיטראקה] טיטרוקה D, טיטרארקה EF; הורודוס] הורדוס B.

verses.translation: And he said{H559} to his servants{H5650}: Behold{H2009}, I believe{H539} that these{H428} wonders{H6382} Yochanan{H3110} the Immerser{H2881} is doing{H6213}.

greek_deviations: The Shem Tov text has NO resurrection clause: Greek Matthew reads 'This is John the Baptist; he is RISEN FROM THE DEAD, and therefore mighty works do shew forth themselves in him.' The Hebrew has only 'Behold, I believe that these wonders Yochanan the Immerser is doing' — Herod credits the wonders to Yochanan without a word about his rising, and the story of his death then follows as a flashback (v. 3, 'this happened because...'). The Vat. Ebr. 100 Hebrew Matthew carries the clause ('who returned to life'), with the Greek.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (14:2): המטביל] omit E; הפלאות] הפעולות A, הנפלאות DG.

verses.translation: This happened because Herodos had seized{H8610} Yochanan{H3110} in those{H1992} days{H3117} and bound him{H631} in prison{H612}, because he was reproving him{H3198} that he should not take{H3947} Ordisa for a wife{H802}, for she was the wife of his brother{H251}.

one_way_hebrew: מוכיחו (H3198, yakach) — 'reproving him': the same covenant-reproof verb as 11:1 (Lev 19:17, הוכח תוכיח); the Immerser does to the king exactly what the Torah commands toward a sinning brother. And the charge is Lev 18:16 / 20:21 — the brother's wife — stated in the Torah's own terms (אשת אחיו).
ויאסרהו (H631) — 'bound him,' the verb of Joseph's imprisonment (Gen 40:3); with בית הסוהר at v. 10 the whole episode is told in Joseph-narrative vocabulary.
textual_notes: The scan reads בימים ההם; the circulating transcription's מימים is a typo, corrected here. The scan spells the name לאורדיסא (ending aleph); the transcription's לאורדיסה is normalized to the printed form.
Howard's apparatus (14:3): לאורדיסא] לאורדישא AB, לאורדיטא D, לאורדישה EF, לאורדיסה G.

verses.translation: And Yochanan{H3110} was saying{H559} to him: She is not fitting for you.

translation_notes: אינה ראויה לך — 'she is not FITTING for you': the rabbinic idiom ראוי ('fit, permitted'), the halakhist's word for what the law allows; Greek οὐκ ἔξεστίν σοι ('it is not lawful for thee') translates the same legal judgment.

verses.translation: And behold{H2009}, Herodos was wishing{H7521} to kill him{H2026}, were it not{H3884} for the fear{H3374} of the people{H5971}, for he was as a prophet{H5030} among them{H996}.

one_way_hebrew: לולי (H3884) — 'were it not for': classical biblical Hebrew (Gen 31:42; Ps 27:13; 124:1-2), a particle rabbinic prose had largely dropped — the author writes in the Bible's own register.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (14:5): לולי] לולא AG; והנה] omit EF.

verses.translation: And at the feast{H4960} of the birthday{H3205} of Herodos, he called{H7121} the great ones{H1419} of the kingdom{H4438} to eat{H398} with him; and while they were eating, his daughter{H1323} was dancing{H7540} among them{H996}, and it pleased{H3190} Herodos.

one_way_hebrew: ובמשתה יום הולד את הורודוס — the construction is Gen 40:20 verbatim in structure: יום הלדת את פרעה ('the birthday of Pharaoh — a feast for all his servants'), down to the untranslatable את before the name, which the base preserves and the other mss smooth away. The author narrates Herod's feast in the Hebrew of Pharaoh's — the only other royal birthday in Scripture, and there too the feast costs a prisoner his head (the baker hanged, Gen 40:22).
מרקדת (H7540) — the girl dances with the very verb of 11:17 ('we sang to you and you did not dance') — Herod's court completes the children's game grimly.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (14:6): את] omit ABDEFG; הולד] הולדת ABDEFG; ביניהם] לפנהם AEF ('before them').

verses.translation: And he swore{H7650} to her that he would give{H5414} her all{H3605} that she would ask{H7592} of him.

textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (14:7): וישבע] ונשבע ABDEFG; את] omit ABDEFG.

verses.translation: And the girl{H5291}, instructed{H3256} by her mother, asked{H7592} for the head{H7218} of Yochanan{H3110} the Immerser{H2881} in one basin{H101}.

one_way_hebrew: אגן (H101) — 'basin': the Sinai covenant-basins (Exod 24:6, ויקח משה חצי הדם וישם באגנת) — a sacrificial vessel; the prophet's blood is served at a king's table in the Torah's covenant-bowl word. Greek πίνακι ('platter') is tableware.
translation_notes: מיומה — as the base prints ('from her day'?); all other mss read מאמה, 'BY HER MOTHER' (so the Greek and Howard: 'instructed by (her mother)'), which the translation follows — a מ/י slip inside Hebrew transmission.
א״ — the ms abbreviates אחד ('one') with gershayim after באגן; F omits it.
textual_notes: The scan reads המטביל; the circulating transcription's המתביל is a typo, corrected here.
Howard's apparatus (14:8): מיומה] מאמה ABDEFG; המטביל] omit F; א״] omit F.

verses.translation: And the king{H4428} was greatly{H3966} grieved{H6087} because of{H1157} the oath{H7621} which he made{H6213} before{H6440} the invited ones{H7121}, and he commanded{H6680} that it be done{H6213} so.

one_way_hebrew: נעצב (H6087) — the grief-verb of Gen 6:6 and 2 Sam 19:3; הקרואים — 'the called ones,' the banquet-guests of 1 Sam 9:13,22 and 1 Kgs 1:41,49 (Adonijah's doomed feast) — the Hebrew reader hears a king's table where invitations end in blood.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (14:9): שעשה...הקרואים] omit F; בעד] + זה G.

verses.translation: And he sent{H7971} to slaughter{H7819} Yochanan{H3110} in the prison-house{H5470}.

one_way_hebrew: בית הסוהר (H5470) — the Joseph narrative's own term for the prison (Gen 39:20-23; 40:3,5), found nowhere else in Scripture: the righteous man bound in the beit ha-sohar under a capricious ruler. Greek φυλακή is generic.

לשחוט (H7819) — 'to SLAUGHTER': the sacrificial verb (Gen 22:10, the Akedah's knife; Exod 12:6, the Pesach lamb) — not 'behead' (Greek ἀπεκεφάλισεν): the Hebrew states the prophet's death as a slaughtering.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (14:10): יוחנן] ליוחנן ABDEFG.

verses.translation: And they brought{H935} the head{H7218} of Yochanan{H3110} in the basin{H101} and gave it{H5414} to the girl{H5291}, and the girl gave{H5414} it to her mother{H517}.

textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (14:11): נתנה] נתנהו A; לאמה] לאמו A.

verses.translation: And the disciples{H8527} of Yochanan{H3110} came{H935} and carried{H5375} the body{H1610} and buried it{H6912}, and the disciples told{H5046} the matter{H1697} to Yeshua{H3442}.

textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (14:12): תלמידי יוחנן] תלמידיו G.

verses.translation: And when Yeshua{H3442} heard{H8085} it, he journeyed{H5265} from there{H8033} in a boat{H591} and went{H1980} to the wilderness{H4057} of Yehudah{H3063}; and when the crowds{H2267} heard, they went after him{H310} from all the provinces{H4082}.

greek_deviations: The Hebrew names the destination — מדבר יהודה, 'the wilderness of JUDEA' (the title-phrase of Ps 63:1, 'A Psalm of David, when he was in the wilderness of Judah') — where Greek has only 'a desert place apart.' And מדינות ('provinces,' Esther's word, H4082) for the Greek's 'cities.'
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (14:13): יהודה] יודא BCDG (the same defective spelling as 24:16); וילכו] הלכו A.

verses.translation: And when they went out{H3318}, he saw{H7200} behind him{H310} a numerous{H7227} people{H5971}, and he extended{H5186} kindness{H2617} to them and healed{H7495} all their diseases{H4245}.

one_way_hebrew: ויט אליו חסד — 'he EXTENDED CHESED to them': Gen 39:21 verbatim (ויט אליו חסד — what YHWH did for Joseph IN THE BEIT HA-SOHAR). Four verses after the prophet is slaughtered in the בית הסוהר (v. 10), the text answers with the prison-narrative's own mercy-idiom. Greek ἐσπλαγχνίσθη ('was moved with compassion') is an emotion; ויט חסד is a covenant act, and it is Joseph's.
מחלה (H4245) — Exod 23:25's promise-word: 'I will take sickness (מחלה) away from the midst of thee.'

verses.translation: And at evening{H6153} time{H6256} his disciples{H8527} drew near{H7126} to him and said{H559} to him: This{H2088} place{H4725} is cramped{H6862} and the hour passing{H5674}; let the crowds{H2267} go{H5800} into the towers{H4026} and take{H3947} what they need for themselves.

translation_notes: במגדלים — 'into the TOWERS' (מגדל, H4026): in medieval Hebrew usage, the fortified villages around a district (Howard: 'into the towers'); Greek has κώμας ('villages'). צר עובר — 'cramped, passing': Howard renders 'limited (and the time) is advancing,' with ms G supplying והעת ('and the time').
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (14:15): צר] + והעת G; הצורך] הצריך G; אליו] + כל A.

verses.translation: And Yeshua{H3442} answered{H6030} them: They have no{H369} need to go{H1980}; give{H5414} them to eat{H398}.

textual_notes: The scan reads ויען; the circulating transcription's ועין is a typo, corrected here.
Howard's apparatus (14:16): להם 1°] + אתם A ('YOU give them').

verses.translation: And they answered{H6030}: We have nothing here except{H518} five{H2568} loaves{H3603} and two{H8147} fish{H1709}.

one_way_hebrew: ככרות (H3603) — 'round loaves' (ככר לחם, 1 Sam 2:36; Jer 37:21 — the daily loaf from the bakers' street given to imprisoned Jeremiah); native bread-Hebrew.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (14:17): שני] ושני ABCDEFG.

verses.translation: And he said{H559} to them: Bring{H935} them to me{H413}.

textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (14:18): להם] omit A.

verses.translation: And he commanded{H6680} that the people{H5971} should sit{H3427} on the grass{H6212}; and when they sat he took{H3947} the five{H2568} loaves{H3603} and the two{H8147} fish{H1709}, and looking{H5027} to the heavens{H8064} he blessed{H1288} them and divided them{H2505} and gave them{H5414} to his disciples{H8527}, and the disciples distributed{H2505} to the companies.

one_way_hebrew: ברך — 'he BLESSED': the Hebrew grace over bread (as Melchizedek blessed, Gen 14:19; cf. 1 Sam 9:13, 'he doth bless the sacrifice; and afterwards they eat'). סייעות — 'companies' (siyya), rabbinic Hebrew for seated groups; the scene is a Hebrew meal in Hebrew words.
textual_notes: The scan reads לקח; the circulating transcription's לחק is a typo, corrected here.
Howard's apparatus (14:19): שישובו] שישבו ABCDEFG; חלקו] + אותם G.

verses.translation: And they all ate{H398} and were satisfied{H7646} — and likewise of the fish{H1709} they ate as they desired{H7522} — and after{H310} they finished{H3615} they took{H3947} the fragments{H6595} that remained{H7604} and filled{H4390} twelve{H8147}{H6240} seahs{H5429} with them.

one_way_hebrew: ואכלו... וישבעו — 'they ate and were satisfied': Deut 8:10's own pair (ואכלת ושבעת, 'thou shalt eat and be satisfied, and bless YHWH') — the blessing (v. 19) and the satisfaction enact the Torah's meal-formula in order.

פתיתים (H6595) — 'fragments': the broken pieces (פתות אתה פתים) of the minchah, Lev 2:6; and סאים — the seah again (Gen 18:6; cf. 13:33): the leftovers are measured in the Torah's own dry measure, where Greek has κοφίνους ('baskets').
textual_notes: The scan reads הפתיתים; the circulating transcription's הפיתיתים is a typo, corrected here.
Howard's apparatus (14:20): וכן] omit DG.

verses.translation: And the number{H4557} of those eating{H398} was five{H2568} thousand{H505} men{H582}, apart from{H905} the women{H802} and the little ones{H2945}.

one_way_hebrew: מלבד הנשים והטף — the census-formula of the Exodus: 'six hundred thousand on foot that were men, beside the little ones' (לבד מטף, Exod 12:37). The wilderness feeding is counted exactly as the Exodus multitude was — men apart from women and taf — and טף is the same household word as 24:45 and 13:52.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (14:21): חמשת] חמש AEFG; מלבד] לבד BDEFG.

verses.translation: And after{H310} this{H2088} he commanded{H6680} his disciples{H8527} to gather{H3664} into the boat{H591} and go on before{H6924} him to the city{H5892} where the crowds{H2267} were going{H1980}.

greek_deviations: Greek Matthew sends the boat 'to the other side, while he sent the multitudes away'; the Hebrew sends the disciples ahead בעיר שהחבורות הולכות — 'to the city where the crowds were going' — the crowds are not dismissed into nowhere but walking to a known town, and the disciples precede him there.
textual_notes: The scan reads בעיר; the circulating transcription's מעיר is a typo, corrected here.
Howard's apparatus (14:22): ואחרי זה] ואחר כן EF; לכנס] ליכנס ADEF; וישליחו] וילכו אותם A.

verses.translation: And after{H310} he left{H5800} the crowds{H2267}, he went up{H5927} to the mountain{H2022} and prayed{H6419} alone{H905}; and at evening{H6153} time{H6256} he was standing{H5975} alone.

one_way_hebrew: עלה להר... לבדו — 'went up to the mountain... alone': Moses' posture (Exod 24:2, 'Moses ALONE shall come near'; Exod 34:3). The Hebrew adds עומד — 'STANDING' alone at evening — the prayer-stance (as Abraham 'stood' before YHWH, Gen 18:22).

verses.translation: And the boat{H591} was in the midst of the sea{H3220}, and the waves{H1530} were driving{H1765} it, because the wind{H7307} was contrary{H5048}.

one_way_hebrew: דוחפות (H1765, dachaph) — 'driving, thrusting': Esther's hurried couriers (Esth 3:15; 8:14); late-biblical Hebrew in living use.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (14:24): באמצע] בלב G ('in the HEART of the sea,' Exod 15:8's בלב ים); the mss vary on וגליהם (גלי הים D, והגלים AB).

verses.translation: At the fourth{H7243} watch{H4931} of the night{H3915} Yeshua{H3442} came{H935} to them, walking{H1980} on the sea{H3220}.

one_way_hebrew: משמרה — the night-watch of Exod 14:24: 'in the morning WATCH (באשמרת הבקר) YHWH looked upon the host of the Egyptians' — the Tanakh's other watch-of-the-night sea event; mss ADG read לאשמורת, Exodus's own form. And הולך בים — 'walking on the sea' — is Job 9:8's credo, 'who alone... treadeth upon the waves of the sea' (דורך על במתי ים): in Hebrew the scene quotes the Creator's job description.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (14:25): למשמרה] לאשמורת ADG, לאשמורה B, ולאשמורות EF; הרביעית] הרביעי AG.

verses.translation: And when his disciples{H8527} saw him{H7200} walking{H1980} on the sea{H3220}, they were terrified{H926}, thinking{H2803} that he was a demon{H7700}, and from the greatness{H7230} of their fear{H6343} they were crying out{H6817}.

translation_notes: נבהלו בשר — the base adds בשר ('flesh'?) after 'they were terrified'; mss ABCG omit it, Howard leaves it untranslated, and G's בשד ('by a demon') suggests it is a corrupt doublet of שד. Retained as printed.
שד (H7700) — 'a DEMON' (Deut 32:17's word again, cf. 11:18), where Greek has φάντασμα ('a phantom'): the disciples' fear is named in Torah vocabulary, not Greek ghost-lore.
textual_notes: The scan reads תלמידיו; the circulating transcription's תלמידים is a typo, corrected here.
Howard's apparatus (14:26): בשר] omit ABCG; הלך] הולך ABDEFG; בחושבם] וחשבוהו ABDEF; היו] היה A.

verses.translation: And then{H227} Yeshua{H3442} answered{H6030} them and said{H559} to them: Let there be faith{H530} in you, for I am he{H1931} — and do not fear{H3372}.

greek_deviations: Greek: 'Be of good cheer (θαρσεῖτε); it is I; be not afraid.' Hebrew: יהיה אמונה בכם שאני הוא — 'let there be FAITH in you, for I AM HE.' The call is to emunah, not courage, and it stands first; and אני הוא is the divine self-declaration of Deut 32:39 and Isa 43:10 — 'that ye may know and BELIEVE me, and understand that I AM HE (אני הוא)' — where faith and ani-hu stand together exactly as here. The Greek's ἐγώ εἰμι translates the formula; the Hebrew speaks it.
textual_notes: The scan reads ויאמר להם; the circulating transcription's להעם is a typo, corrected here.
Howard's apparatus (14:27): ואז] אז G; אמונה בכם] transposed EF; ואל] אל AEFG.

verses.translation: And Petros answered{H6030} and said{H559} to him: Master{H113}, if{H518} you are he{H1931}, command{H6680} me to come{H935} to you on the water{H4325}.

translation_notes: אדו׳ — the ms abbreviates אדוני ('my master') with a geresh; at v. 30 the scan even prints it run together with the next word (אדו׳הושיעני).
textual_notes: The scan reads ויען פייט״רוס ויאמר לו; the circulating transcription dropped ויאמר לו, restored here.
Howard's apparatus (14:28): אותי לבא] omit EF; פייטרוס] פיטרו A, פיטרוש BDG.

verses.translation: And Yeshua{H3442} said{H559} to him: Come{H935}. And Petros went down{H3381} from the ship{H5600} and walked{H1980} on the sea{H3220} and came{H935} to Yeshua{H3442}.

one_way_hebrew: וירד... מהספינה — the text switches from אניה (vv. 13, 22, 24) to ספינה (H5600) at exactly this point — and ספינה occurs once in all Scripture: Jonah 1:5, where Jonah 'was gone DOWN (ירד) into the sides of the ship.' A man going down out of the sefinah into the sea is Jonah's scene rewritten — this time in faith instead of flight. The word-switch is invisible in Greek (πλοῖον both times; the transcriber's own footnote asks why the word changes).
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (14:29): בים] במים G; פיטרוס] פיטרו A, פיטרוש BDG.

verses.translation: But when he saw{H7200} the strength{H2392} of the wind{H7307}, he feared{H6342} greatly{H3966}, and as he began{H2490} to sink{H2883} he cried out{H6817} and said{H559}: Master{H113}, save me{H3467}!

one_way_hebrew: ליטבע... הושיעני — Psalm 69 in two words: 'Save me (הושיעני), O God; for the waters are come in unto my soul. I SINK (טבעתי) in deep mire... let me be delivered... out of the deep waters' (Ps 69:2-3,15). Peter's cry is the Psalmist's, verb for verb (טבע H2883, ישע H3467); Greek κύριε, σῶσόν με translates the prayer without its address in the Psalter.
textual_notes: The scan reads הרוח; the circulating transcription's חרוח is a typo, corrected here. The scan prints אדו׳הושיעני run together (the transcriber's footnote queries the spacing); the abbreviation אדו׳ = אדוני.

verses.translation: And immediately Yeshua{H3442} stretched out{H748} his hand{H3027} and took him{H3947}, and said{H559} to him: Man{H120} of little faith{H530}, why{H4100} did you doubt?

one_way_hebrew: נסתפקת — 'you doubted': the rabbinic legal term ספק (safek, a doubt), in its reflexive verb — the Hebrew of the study-house (the transcriber's footnote calls it 'a curious way to translate ὀλιγόπιστε' — it is not a translation; it is the native idiom the Greek ἐδίστασας renders). אדם מאמונה מעוטה — 'man of LITTLE faith,' the same smallness-of-faith idiom as 13:58 (למיעוט אמונתם).
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (14:31): אדם] זה G.

verses.translation: And when they went up{H5927} into the boat{H591}, the wind{H7307} rested{H5117}.

one_way_hebrew: נח הרוח — 'the wind RESTED' (נוח, H5117, Noach's own verb, Gen 8:4): the storm ends in the vocabulary of the ark coming to rest; Greek ἐκόπασεν ('grew weary') has no share in it.
textual_notes: The scan reads הרוח; the circulating transcription's חרוח is a typo, corrected here.

verses.translation: And those who were in the ship{H5600} bowed down{H7812} to him and said{H559}: In truth{H571} you are the Son{H1121} of Elohim{H430}.

translation_notes: ms writes האלקים with the reverent ק-spelling (as at 12:4).
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (14:33): האלקים] אלקים A, האלים F.

Greek 14:34 ('And when they were gone over, they came into the land of Gennesaret') has no counterpart in the Shem Tov text: Howard notes that ALL mss lack v. 34, and the text runs directly from v. 33 to v. 35 (his English numbers the next verse 34). The Vat. Ebr. 100 Hebrew Matthew has the verse ('they reached the land at Ginneisaret').

verses.translation: And when the men{H582} of the place{H4725} recognized him{H5234}, they sent{H7971} into all that kingdom{H4438} and brought{H935} to him all the sick{H2470} of all diseases{H4064}.

one_way_hebrew: מדוים (H4064, madveh) — Deut 28:60's word for the diseases of Egypt (כל מדוה מצרים): the healings undo the covenant-curse by name.
textual_notes: The scan reads כל החולים; the circulating transcription's צל is a typo, corrected here.
Howard's apparatus (14:35): מכל] + מיני ABCDG ('of all KINDS of diseases'); אותו] אותה CDEFG; מכל מדוים] omit EF.

verses.translation: And they entreated{H2470} his face{H6440}, that he might be pleased{H7521} to allow them{H5800} to touch{H5060} the wing{H3671} of his robe{H4598}; and every one who touched{H5060} it was healed{H7495}.

one_way_hebrew: וחלו פניו — 'they ENTREATED HIS FACE': the Tanakh's supplication idiom (חלה פנים — Exod 32:11, Moses entreating the face of YHWH; Ps 45:13; Mal 1:9). Greek παρεκάλουν is bare asking; the Hebrew is the temple-idiom of seeking the face.

בכנף מעילו — 'the WING of his ROBE': 1 Sam 15:27's exact phrase (בכנף מעילו — the robe-corner of Samuel that Saul seized), the kanaph in which Israel wears the tzitzit (Num 15:38, על כנפי בגדיהם) and in which Malachi promised healing — 'the sun of righteousness shall arise with HEALING IN ITS WINGS (בכנפיה)' (Mal 3:20). In Hebrew, touching the kanaph and being healed IS Mal 3:20 enacted; Greek κρασπέδου ('fringe') keeps the ritual object and loses the wing, the verse, and the promise.

chapter_notes.summary: Matthew 14 in the Shem Tov Hebrew tells the Baptizer's death and the sea-walking in the Tanakh's own scenes. (1) 14:2 has NO resurrection clause — Herod says only 'I believe that these wonders Yochanan the Immerser is doing,' where Greek Matthew has 'he is risen from the dead'; Vat. Ebr. 100 sides with the Greek. (2) 14:34 is missing from ALL Shem Tov mss (Howard's note); the text runs from v. 33 to v. 35. (3) The Yochanan narrative is written in Joseph-narrative Hebrew: בית הסוהר (14:10, Gen 39-40's prison, nowhere else in Scripture), ויאסרהו (14:3), and then ויט אליו חסד (14:14) — Gen 39:21 verbatim, YHWH's kindness to Joseph IN the beit ha-sohar; and Herod's feast (14:6) is built on Gen 40:20's יום הלדת את פרעה down to the preserved את. (4) 14:10 says the prophet was SLAUGHTERED (לשחוט, the sacrificial verb), served in the covenant-basin אגן (Exod 24:6). (5) The sea-walk speaks Scripture: the fourth WATCH recalls Exod 14:24's morning-watch sea event; walking on the sea is Job 9:8's credo; 14:27 reads 'let there be FAITH in you, for I AM HE (אני הוא)' — Deut 32:39/Isa 43:10's self-declaration where Greek has 'be of good cheer'; Peter goes DOWN from the ספינה (14:29) — Jonah 1:5's word, its only occurrence in Scripture — and sinks with Ps 69's own verbs (ליטבע... הושיעני, 14:30); the wind 'RESTS' (נח, Noach's verb, 14:32). (6) 14:31's 'why did you doubt' is the rabbinic נסתפקת (safek) — study-house Hebrew. (7) 14:36: they entreat his FACE (חלה פנים, Exod 32:11) to touch בכנף מעילו — 1 Sam 15:27's exact phrase — and are healed: Mal 3:20's 'healing in its wings' enacted; Greek 'fringe' loses the kanaph. (8) 14:21 counts the crowd by the Exodus census-formula (מלבד הנשים והטף, Exod 12:37), and 14:20's 'ate and were satisfied' is Deut 8:10. (9) Vernacular/loan layer continues: טיטרא״קה (tetrarka) flagged with gershayim as foreign; מדבר יהודה named where Greek has 'a desert place.' Shem Tov's section divisions fall at vv. 1 (Perek 65) and 22 (66).
